name: Link Purpose (Link Only)
explanation: This is a stricter version of SC 2.4.4: a link's purpose must be clear from its link text alone, without needing any surrounding sentence, paragraph, or list context to understand it. Where the Level A criterion allows context like a nearby heading or sentence to fill in the meaning, this AAA criterion requires the link text itself to be self-sufficient, so it would make sense even when read completely out of context, such as in a screen reader's standalone list of all links on a page.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users who pull up a page's link list to navigate quickly see only the link text stripped of its surrounding context, so this criterion ensures that list is meaningful on its own rather than a page full of identical or vague entries like "read more." This benefits any user scanning a page's links out of context, including sighted users skimming a printed link reference or a browser extension that lists links separately from the page content.

codeExample.bad:
New accessibility guidelines released

The W3C has published updated guidance...

Read more
codeExample.good:
New accessibility guidelines released

The W3C has published updated guidance...

Read the full article on the new accessibility guidelines

howToTest: Extract just the visible text of every link on the page, as if you were reading them from a bare list with no surrounding sentences, headings, or paragraphs. For each one, ask whether its purpose is clear from that text alone. If a link only makes sense because of a nearby heading or sentence, such as a bare "Read more" that depends on the article title above it, this stricter AAA criterion fails even though the Level A version might pass.

check.question: A page has a link reading "Learn more about our return policy" that appears directly below a paragraph about shipping. Does this link satisfy SC 2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only)?
choices: Yes, because the link text itself names its destination clearly without needing surrounding context
No, because the link relies on the shipping paragraph above it for meaning
Yes, because it's part of the same page as the shipping information
It depends only on whether the link is underlined
